question: According to the handbook, what does alcohol do to a driver?
choices: Reduces alertness, interferes with judgment, and impairs vision
Affects reaction time only, leaving judgment intact
Impairs vision only after the legal limit is reached
Slows the body but sharpens concentration
explanation: The handbook lists three effects together: alcohol reduces alertness, interferes with judgment, and impairs vision. Judgment is included deliberately — the ability you would use to decide whether you are safe to drive is itself damaged, which is why self-assessment after drinking is unreliable.

question: What happens to blood alcohol concentration when someone has more than one drink per hour?
choices: It builds up in the body and can keep rising after the last drink
It levels off automatically after the second drink
It falls steadily as soon as drinking stops
It stays constant until the body has processed all food
explanation: The handbook explains that BAC builds up when drinks come faster than one per hour, and gives an example where BAC is still above 0.06 percent at 4 a.m. after a last drink at 11:30 p.m. This is why someone can be more impaired later than when they stopped drinking.

question: A driver has her last drink at 11:30 p.m. and sleeps for a few hours. Why might she still be arrested for DUI at 4 a.m.?

Sleeping prevents the body from processing alcohol at all

explanation: This is the handbook's own worked example: with a last drink at 11:30 p.m., BAC keeps increasing and is still above 0.06 percent at 4 a.m. Someone at that level can be arrested for DUI. Sleeping a few hours is not the same as being sober.

question: Which statement about how alcohol affects people is correct?
choices: It affects a person differently at different times, depending on physical and emotional condition, other drugs and food
It affects everyone identically for a given body weight
It has no effect until the third drink
Its effect depends only on the type of drink consumed
explanation: The handbook says alcohol affects a person differently at different times, and names physical and emotional conditions, other drugs, and even the amount of food in the stomach as things that change the effect. question: Under West Virginia's zero tolerance law, what happens to a driver under 21 found with any measurable alcohol in their system?
choices: They will lose their driver's license
They receive a warning for a first occurrence
Nothing, provided their BAC is under 0.08
They are fined but keep their license
explanation: West Virginia has a zero tolerance law for drivers under 21. The handbook states that if any amount of alcohol is found in the system of a driver under 21, that driver will lose their license. The adult 0.08 threshold does not apply to them.

question: A 19-year-old is stopped and tests at a BAC well below 0.08. What is the consequence in West Virginia?

No action, because they are below the 0.08 limit
A warning only, because the limit applies equally to all ages
The license is suspended only if they refuse the test
explanation: The 0.08 figure is the adult presumption of driving under the influence. For a driver under 21 the zero tolerance law applies instead: any measurable alcohol means losing the license. Being under 0.08 is no defence for an underage driver.

Grounds for a fine but never a revocation

question: What is the consequence of refusing the Breathalyzer after a DUI arrest in West Virginia?
choices: Your privilege to operate a motor vehicle is revoked for one year and up to life
Nothing, since the test is voluntary
A fine, but your license is unaffected
A 30-day suspension only

question: Your tire blows out at highway speed. What should you do first?
choices: Hold the wheel tightly, steer straight ahead, and ease up on the accelerator
Brake hard immediately to slow down as fast as possible
Steer sharply onto the shoulder straight away
Pull the parking brake to stop the vehicle quickly
explanation: A blowout has already upset the car's balance, and braking makes it worse. The handbook says to hold tightly to the steering wheel, steer straight ahead and ease up on the accelerator, and not to brake until the vehicle is under control. Only then pull all the way off the road.

choices: Not until the vehicle is under control
Immediately, as hard as possible
Only once you have already left the roadway
Only after shifting into neutral
explanation: The handbook is explicit: do not brake until the vehicle is under control. Braking while the car is still unstable from a blown tire can turn a recoverable situation into a loss of control. Get it straight and slowed first, then brake and pull off.

Water conducts electricity from the battery
Water causes the tires to explode

Keep driving to the nearest service station regardless of distance
Remove the radiator cap at once to release pressure
Turn the heater off and continue at highway speed

question: How does the handbook suggest preventing overheating in slow-moving traffic?

Switch the engine off at every stop
Drive in the highest gear available
Open the hood while stopped in traffic
explanation: The handbook describes shifting into neutral and racing the engine briefly during stops, which speeds up the fan and water pump and moves more air and coolant through the system while the vehicle is not moving fast enough to do it naturally.

Turn off the ignition immediately while still at speed
Apply the parking brake at full force
Steer onto the shoulder without slowing
explanation: The order matters. Concentrate on steering and keep your eyes on the road, try to free the pedal with your foot, and if that does not work push in the clutch or shift into neutral. Only then use the brakes, stop at the nearest safe place, and turn off the ignition.

Immediately, before doing anything else
As soon as the clutch is pushed in
Never — the ignition should be left running
explanation: The handbook puts turning off the ignition last: use your brakes, stop at the nearest safe place, and turn off the ignition. Killing the engine while still moving can cost you power steering and power brakes at the worst moment.

To signal other drivers that you have recovered
To engage the anti-lock braking system

Every two years regardless of wear
When they are more than half worn
Only when a tire fails inspection

Water freezes more readily after dark
Emergency services do not operate at night
Headlights cause water to appear shallower than it is
explanation: The handbook notes flooded roadways are especially dangerous at night when it is much more difficult to see. Combined with the fact that the road surface may already have eroded away beneath the water, this is why the instruction is never to attempt a crossing.

Use high engine speed to break traction free
Start in the highest available gear at full throttle
Accelerate hard briefly, then lift off
explanation: The handbook says to keep your engine speed low when starting on snow or ice and to accelerate slowly and smoothly, letting the clutch out slowly in a manual. It then suggests testing the brakes while driving slowly to judge how slippery the road is.

Hold the brake pedal down firmly and steer
Use the parking brake to steer
Steering while braking is impossible in any vehicle

The inspection station's, until the sticker expires
The DMV's, through random roadside checks
The insurer's, as a condition of coverage
explanation: The handbook says plainly that it is up to you to keep your vehicle in proper driving condition, then lists the common defects that cause crashes. The two-yearly inspection is a minimum check, not a substitute for maintaining the vehicle.

In the driver's seat with the engine off
Asleep in the vehicle for at least an hour
Anywhere, provided it lasts ten minutes

Open the window and continue to your destination
Increase speed to arrive sooner
Continue but reduce following distance to stay engaged

Keep your hand over the horn
Watch the vehicle's brake lights exclusively

Rear-end crashes only
Head-on crashes only
Rollover crashes

Inattention

Before entering the intersection, where you can see traffic from all directions

Proceed, since you already made a legal stop

Give the right-of-way to the traffic you are merging with

A weight-restricted bridge
A work zone flagger

You are approaching a construction or maintenance work area
The warning has expired
The sign is a guide sign, not a warning

White on green

White on brown

question: You want to know which services are available at the next exit. Which sign colour do you look for?

Black on white
White on blue
White on green
explanation: Motorist services signs are white on blue, while green signs handle navigation and brown signs mark parks and recreation areas.

question: A white-on-brown sign appears beside the highway. What is it for?

A hospital
A construction detour
A park or public recreation area
explanation: Signs for parks and public recreation areas are white on brown, distinguishing them at a glance from green navigation signs and blue service signs.

question: Black letters on white bars in the shape of an X at a railroad crossing is called a:

Pennant
Crossbar
Chevron
explanation: The handbook names the X-shaped sign of white bars with black letters a crossbuck; it marks the crossing itself.

question: What does a sign mounted below the crossbuck tell you?
choices: The distance to the next crossing
The number of tracks, when there are two or more
The speed of approaching trains
The name of the railroad
explanation: A sign below the crossbuck indicates the number of tracks when there are two or more, which is a warning that a second train may be coming on the other set.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which of these is NOT a form the handbook gives for railroad crossing signs?

A white crossbuck with black letters
An orange rectangle with black letters
A round yellow sign with black symbols
explanation: Railroad crossing signs may be round or diamond shaped, yellow with black symbols, or a white crossbuck with black letters; orange is the work zone colour.

source.sourceQuote: Railroad crossing signs can be round or diamond shaped, yellow with black symbols, or  black letters on white bars in the shape of an X called a crossbuck.

question: At a railroad crossing you must yield to:
choices: Only trains sounding a horn
Trains only when the gate is down
All trains
Only passenger trains
explanation: The rule is unqualified: you must yield to all trains, and a train cannot stop or swerve for you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must yield to all trains.  Failure to stop when lights are fl ashing, or a barrier is down, will result in a citation.

question: The lights at a crossing begin flashing but you cannot see a train yet. What happens if you drive across?
choices: Nothing, as long as no train is visible
It is allowed if you first stop
It is allowed if the gates have not lowered
It will result in a citation
explanation: Failure to stop when lights are flashing, or when a barrier is down, will result in a citation — the signals, not your own sight of the train, control.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must yield to all trains.  Failure to stop when lights are fl ashing, or a barrier is down, will result in a citation.

question: You have waited for a train to clear a crossing that carries two sets of tracks. What should you do before moving off?
choices: Check for a second train on the other set of tracks
Move off as soon as the last car passes
Follow the vehicle ahead closely to clear the queue
Sound your horn to warn any approaching train
explanation: Where there are two or more tracks the handbook warns you to be alert for a second train on the other set, which the first train can hide until it has passed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When there are two (2) or more tracks, you must be alert for a second train on the other set of tracks.

question: Traffic is backed up beyond a railroad crossing. When may you move onto the tracks?
choices: Never, while other vehicles are on the far side
Only when the vehicle ahead has moved far enough that you can clear the tracks
As soon as the gates are up, regardless of the queue
Whenever the vehicle ahead begins to move
explanation: You should not enter a crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough that you can clear the tracks; otherwise you may be trapped on them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you should not enter a railroad crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough ahead that you can clear the tracks.  Otherwise, you may be trapped on the tracks and hit by another vehicle or by a train.

question: Why does the handbook warn against entering a crossing before you can clear it?
choices: Your vehicle may stall on the rails
The gates may damage your vehicle
You may be trapped on the tracks and hit by another vehicle or by a train
You may be fined for obstructing the railroad
explanation: The stated reason is that you may be trapped on the tracks and hit by another vehicle or by a train, with nowhere to go once the queue stops moving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you should not enter a railroad crossing until the vehicle ahead has moved far enough ahead that you can clear the tracks.  Otherwise, you may be trapped on the tracks and hit by another vehicle or by a train.

question: Facing a circular green signal, a driver may:
choices: Enter the intersection and go straight, turn right or turn left unless other devices prohibit it
Only go straight ahead
Only turn in the direction of the nearest arrow
Proceed without regard to right-of-way rules
explanation: A circular green allows straight, right and left movements unless signs or pavement markings prohibit them, and all turns must still follow right-of-way rules.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Drivers facing this signal may enter the intersection and go straight through, turn right, or left, unless, other traffi  c control devices (signs or pavement markings) prohibit certain movements.

question: You are waiting to turn left on a circular green and two cars are coming the other way. What must you do?
choices: Sound your horn and complete the turn
Yield to the oncoming vehicles before turning
Turn at once, because the green gives you the intersection
Wait for the signal to turn yellow, then turn
explanation: A driver facing a circular green who wishes to turn left must yield to oncoming vehicles; the green permits you into the intersection but does not give you priority over them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A driver who is facing a circular green indication and wishes to turn left must yield to oncoming vehicles.

question: Which statement about a circular green is NOT correct?
choices: It allows a right turn unless a sign prohibits it
Turns made on it must follow accepted right-of-way rules
It gives you the right-of-way over oncoming traffic when turning left
It allows you to enter the intersection
explanation: A circular green does not give a left-turning driver priority: the handbook says that driver must yield to oncoming vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A driver who is facing a circular green indication and wishes to turn left must yield to oncoming vehicles.

question: A green arrow means a driver may:
choices: Stop and wait for a circular green
Enter the intersection to make the movement the arrow shows
Proceed in any direction
Go only if the circular green is also lit
explanation: Drivers facing a green arrow may enter the intersection to make the movement shown by the arrow, whether the arrow is shown alone or with other indications.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A green arrow may be shown alone or with other indications.  Drivers facing the signal may enter the intersection to make the movement shown by the arrow.

question: The left-turn signal ahead of you changes to a green arrow. What does that usually tell you about oncoming traffic?
choices: It is also being given a green arrow
It must yield only if turning
It is stopped
It has the right-of-way
explanation: When the green arrow is shown in a left-turn signal it usually means that opposing traffic is stopped, which is what makes the turn a protected one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When the green arrow is shown in a left-turn signal, it usually means that opposing traffi  c is stopped.

question: A steady circular yellow signal means:
choices: Proceed with caution through the intersection
Stop and remain stopped
The signal is out of order
The green light is ending and will change to red
explanation: A steady circular yellow means the green is ending and will change to red; it is not a caution signal like a flashing yellow.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: This means that the green light is ending and will change to red.  You should only drive through a yellow light if the vehicle clearance is within the intersection.

question: The light changes to steady yellow as you approach the intersection and you are still short of it. What does the handbook direct?
choices: Do not drive through, since you are not already within the intersection
Accelerate to clear the intersection before the red
Continue at the same speed regardless
Stop only if a vehicle is waiting on the cross street
explanation: You should only drive through a yellow light if the vehicle clearance is within the intersection, so a driver still short of it should be stopping rather than speeding up.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: This means that the green light is ending and will change to red.  You should only drive through a yellow light if the vehicle clearance is within the intersection.

question: Which indication tells a driver that a green arrow is about to end?
choices: A red arrow
A yellow arrow
A steady circular yellow
A flashing yellow
explanation: A yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending and will change to red, just as a steady circular yellow ends a circular green.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Yellow Arrow / LEFT TURN - This means that the green arrow is ending and will change to red.

question: Traffic facing a steady circular red signal must:
choices: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop for three seconds and then continue
Stop, unless making a movement permitted by a green arrow
Stop only if cross traffic is present
explanation: A steady circular red requires traffic to stop unless a green arrow permits the movement, and the driver must remain stopped until another indication allows them to proceed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Traffi  c facing a steady circular red signal must stop unless making a movement permitted by a green arrow.  The driver must remain stopped until allowed to proceed by another indication.

question: You have stopped at a steady red. When may you proceed?
choices: After counting to five
As soon as the cross traffic clears
Whenever no pedestrians are in the crosswalk
When another signal indication allows it, or when making a permitted turn on red
explanation: The driver must remain stopped until allowed to proceed by another indication; the only exception the handbook gives is a permitted turn on red.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Traffi  c facing a steady circular red signal must stop unless making a movement permitted by a green arrow.  The driver must remain stopped until allowed to proceed by another indication.

question: A steady red arrow points left at the signal ahead. What must you do?
choices: Come to a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk and stay stopped while it is red
Stop, then turn left when the way is clear
Treat it as a yield and merge into a gap
Proceed if the circular signal beside it is green
explanation: A steady red arrow requires a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk for the direction indicated, and you must remain stopped as long as the signal is red.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Come to a complete stop before reaching the intersection, stop line or cross walk for the direction indicated by the arrow.  Remain stopped as long as the signal is red.

question: Where signs do not prohibit it, a driver facing a red signal may turn:
choices: Right or left at any intersection
Left from any street onto a one-way street
Right only from a one-way street
Right at the intersection of two-way streets, or left from a one-way street onto another one-way street
explanation: The handbook permits a right turn on red at the intersection of two-way streets, and a left on red only from a one-way street to another one-way street.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or may turn left on red from a one-way street to another one-way street.  These turns may be made after yielding to all other traffi  c and pedestrians, and if no signs are posted to prohibit them.

question: You want to turn right on red. What must happen before you go?
choices: A complete stop, then yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians
A slow roll while checking for traffic
Waiting for the signal to flash
Sounding the horn to warn cross traffic
explanation: Turns on red may only be made after yielding to all other traffic and pedestrians, and Chapter VI adds that the driver must first come to a complete stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or may turn left on red from a one-way street to another one-way street.  These turns may be made after yielding to all other traffi  c and pedestrians, and if no signs are posted to prohibit them.

question: Which of these turns on red is NOT permitted by the handbook?
choices: No turn on red at all where a sign prohibits it
A left turn on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street
A right turn on red at the intersection of two-way streets
A left turn on red from a one-way street onto another one-way street
explanation: A left on red is only allowed from a one-way street onto another one-way street; starting from a two-way street is not covered by the rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or may turn left on red from a one-way street to another one-way street.  These turns may be made after yielding to all other traffi  c and pedestrians, and if no signs are posted to prohibit them.

question: At a red signal a sign reads NO TURN ON RED, but the way is completely clear. What may you do?
choices: Turn if no pedestrians are present
Treat the signal as a flashing red
Wait for the green, because the sign prohibits the turn
Turn after a complete stop, since the way is clear
explanation: Turns on red may be made only if no signs are posted to prohibit them, so a posted prohibition removes the option no matter how clear the road looks.

source.sourceQuote: A driver may turn right on red at the intersection of two-way streets, or may turn left on red from a one-way street to another one-way street.  These turns may be made after yielding to all other traffi  c and pedestrians, and if no signs are posted to prohibit them.

question: A circular flashing red signal means the same as:
choices: A green light
A no-passing zone
A stop sign
A yield sign
explanation: A circular flashing red is the same as a stop sign: drivers must come to a complete stop and yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: You face a circular flashing yellow at an intersection. What are you permitted to do?
choices: Stop completely, then go
Stop and wait for a green
Yield only to traffic on your left
Proceed through the intersection with caution
explanation: Drivers facing a circular flashing yellow light may proceed through the intersection with caution; only the flashing red requires a complete stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Drivers facing a circular fl ashing yellow light may proceed through the intersection

question: A power cut has left the signals at a junction flashing instead of cycling. How should you treat them?
choices: The same as intersection flashers
As though the intersection were uncontrolled
As a four-way green
As a closed road
explanation: When signals are not needed or are out of order they may be placed in flashing operation, and the handbook says they then mean the same as intersection flashers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When traffi  c control signals are not needed or are out of order, they may be placed in fl ashing operations. When this happens, they are the same as intersection fl ashers.

question: A hand symbol or DON'T WALK signal tells pedestrians:
choices: That the signal is out of order
Not to cross the crosswalk
To cross quickly
To cross only at the far side
explanation: When the hand symbol or DON'T WALK appears, pedestrians are not to cross the crosswalk.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Hand Symbol or DON'T WALK- when these appear pedestrians are not to cross the crosswalk.

question: Which signal tells a pedestrian it is safe to cross inside the crosswalk lines?
choices: A flashing yellow light
A green arrow
The walking man or WALK
The steady hand symbol
explanation: The walking man or WALK signal means pedestrians are safe to cross the street inside the crosswalk lines; crosswalk signals are traffic signals for pedestrians and must be obeyed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Walking Man or WALK - when these appear  pedestrians are safe to cross the street inside the crosswalk lines.

question: A blind person on foot using a guide dog or carrying a white cane has the right-of-way:
choices: Only when the WALK signal is showing
On a highway, street or road whether or not they are in a crosswalk
Only within a marked crosswalk
Only at signalised intersections
explanation: The handbook gives a blind pedestrian using a guide dog, service animal, white cane or walking stick the right-of-way regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A blind person who is on foot and using a guide dog or other service animal, or is carrying a white cane or walking stick, has the right-of-way on a highway, street, or road regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk or not.

question: A person carrying a white cane steps into the road mid-block, well away from any crosswalk. What must you do?
choices: Sound your horn to warn them back to the kerb
Yield only if a guide dog is present
Yield, because they have the right-of-way regardless of the crosswalk
Proceed, because they are not in a crosswalk
explanation: The right-of-way applies whether or not the person is in a crosswalk, and it covers a white cane or walking stick as well as a guide dog or other service animal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A blind person who is on foot and using a guide dog or other service animal, or is carrying a white cane or walking stick, has the right-of-way on a highway, street, or road regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk or not.

question: White lines on the pavement separate:
choices: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions
The road from the shoulder only
Parking spaces from travel lanes only
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
explanation: White lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction, while yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: WHITE lines separate traffic lanes moving in the SAME direction.

question: You notice the line beside your lane is yellow. What does that tell you about the traffic on the other side of it?
choices: It is moving in the opposite direction
It is moving in the same direction
It is a parking lane
It is a bus-only lane
explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic lanes moving in the opposite direction, which is why crossing one carries a head-on risk that crossing a white line does not.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: YELLOW lines separate traffic lanes moving in the OPPOSITE direction.

question: A broken yellow line on your side of the centre line means:
choices: The lane is reversible
Traffic beside you moves the same way
You may pass when it is safe
You must not pass
explanation: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and if the broken marking is on your side you may pass when it is safe.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.  If this marking is on your side of the road, you may pass when it is safe.

question: The yellow line on your side is broken and a slow truck is ahead, but you cannot see far enough to be sure of oncoming traffic. What should you do?
choices: Pass immediately, since the marking allows it
Pass on the right instead
Sound your horn and pass
Stay behind, because the line permits a pass but does not make one safe
explanation: A broken yellow line means you may pass when it is safe; the marking grants permission but the judgement of safety, including sight distance, is still yours.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Broken yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.  If this marking is on your side of the road, you may pass when it is safe.

question: If a solid yellow line is on your side of the road, you:
choices: Must not pass
May pass when no traffic is coming
May pass if the vehicle ahead is slow
May pass only at night
explanation: The handbook is explicit: if a solid yellow line is on your side of the road, you MUST NOT PASS.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If a solid yellow line is on your side of the road, you MUST NOT PASS.

question: You are halfway through passing a car when the yellow line on your side becomes solid. What does the marking mean?
choices: The solid line only applies to trucks
Sight distance has run out and you must be back in your lane
You may continue as long as the pass has begun
You may stay left until the line becomes broken again
explanation: A solid yellow on your side means no passing, which is why a pass must be planned to finish before the broken line ends.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If a solid yellow line is on your side of the road, you MUST NOT PASS.

question: Where does a solid yellow line NOT mean no passing?
choices: On your side of a two-way road through a curve
On your side of a two-way road over a hill
Marking the left edge of the pavement on an interstate or divided four-lane road
On your side of a two-lane road
explanation: On interstates, one-way streets and divided four-lane roads a solid yellow line marks the left edge of the pavement rather than a no-passing line.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: On interstates, one-way streets, or divided four-lane roads, a solid yellow line will mark the left edge of the pavement.

question: Broken white lines on a roadway indicate:
choices: The edge of the pavement
A lane reserved for buses
Lanes moving in the same direction, which you may cross to change lanes
Lanes moving in opposite directions
explanation: On roadways with more than one lane moving in one direction, the lanes are separated by broken white lines, and you drive within them, crossing only to change lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: On roadways which have more than one (1) lane moving in one direction, traffic lanes are separated by broken white lines.

question: Which of these is NOT permitted where broken white lines separate lanes?
choices: Changing lanes when it is safe
Driving within your lane
Passing where no sign prohibits it
Straddling the line while travelling
explanation: The handbook says to drive within these lines and never straddle them, except when actually changing lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Drive within these lines and never straddle them, except when changing lanes.

question: Two lanes running the same direction are separated by a solid white line. What does it tell you?
choices: Do not change lanes
Change lanes only after signalling
Traffic beside you is oncoming
The lane ends ahead
explanation: When solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, the instruction is DO NOT CHANGE LANES.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Solid white lines mark the edge of the pavement.  At night or in bad weather, they help you stay on the road.  When solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, DO NOT CHANGE LANES.

question: White diamond shapes painted in a lane mean the lane is designated for:
choices: Slow-moving vehicles
Car pools, bicycles or buses
Emergency vehicles only
Left turns from either direction
explanation: White diamonds painted in the roadway inform drivers that the lane is designated for car pools, bicycles or buses.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: White diamond shapes painted in the roadway to inform drivers the lane is designated for car pools, bicycles, or buses.

question: Which pavement marking identifies a special purpose lane?
choices: A wide white line across the lane
Solid yellow lines on both sides
White diamond shapes painted in the lane
A double broken yellow line
explanation: The white diamond is the special purpose lane marking; the double broken yellow marks a reversible lane and the wide white line across the lane is a stop line.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: White diamond shapes painted in the roadway to inform drivers the lane is designated for car pools, bicycles, or buses.

question: A centre left-turn lane may be used for:
choices: Left turns from either direction
Passing slower traffic
Travelling through when your lane is busy
Parking briefly
explanation: Centre left-turn lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are not to be used as through or passing lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Center Left-Turn Lanes - These lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are not to be used as through or passing lanes.

question: Traffic in your lane is crawling and the centre lane marked for left turns is empty. May you use it to get past?
choices: Yes, provided no vehicle is waiting to turn
No — it is not to be used as a through or passing lane
Yes, if you signal first
Yes, if you re-enter your lane within 100 feet
explanation: The centre left-turn lane is reserved for left turns from either direction, and traffic may be entering it head-on from the opposite side at any moment.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Center Left-Turn Lanes - These lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are not to be used as through or passing lanes.

question: How do you recognise a centre left-turn lane?
choices: A double broken yellow line on both sides
Wide white lines painted across it
Solid yellow lines nearest the through lanes with broken lines to the left of them
White diamonds painted along it
explanation: You can recognise these lanes by the solid yellow lines nearest the through lanes and broken lines to the left of them; a double broken yellow on both sides would be a reversible lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Center Left-Turn Lanes - These lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction and are not to be used as through or passing lanes.

question: A wide white line painted across your traffic lane marks:
choices: A pedestrian-only area
The start of a passing zone
Where you must stop your vehicle at an intersection
The edge of the pavement
explanation: Stop lines are wide white lines painted across traffic lanes that mark where you must stop, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stop Lines - Wide white lines, painted across traffic lanes, mark where you must stop your vehicle at intersections.

question: There is no stop line and no crosswalk at the intersection where you must stop. Where do you stop?
choices: With your front wheels level with the kerb line of the cross street
In the intersection, to see better
Wherever the vehicle behind you allows
Before you enter the intersection, where you can see traffic from all directions
explanation: With no stop lines or crosswalks you must stop before entering the intersection, and you should be able to see traffic coming from all directions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If there are no stop lines or crosswalks, you must stop your vehicle before you enter the intersections.

question: Which of these is NOT correct about crosswalk markings?
choices: Every pedestrian crosswalk is marked with white lines
Many crosswalks are marked by solid white lines
Some crosswalks, especially in residential areas, are not marked
You must not block a crosswalk with your car
explanation: Some crosswalks, especially in residential areas, are not marked at all, which is why the stop-sign rule refers to marked or unmarked crosswalks.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Many pedestrian crosswalks are marked by solid white lines. Some crosswalks, especially in residential areas, are not marked.

question: West Virginia law prohibits driving at a speed that is:
choices: Greater than 70 mph anywhere in the state
Greater than reasonable and prudent for existing conditions
Greater than the posted limit, and nothing else
Below the flow of traffic
explanation: Beyond the posted numbers, the law forbids any speed greater than is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions, so conditions can make a posted speed illegal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law prohibits driving at a speed that is greater than reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.

question: You are driving 55 mph on an open county highway posted at 55 when fog cuts visibility sharply. Are you within the law?
choices: Yes, provided your headlights are on
Yes, unless a lower limit is posted for fog
No, because the speed is no longer reasonable and prudent for the conditions
Yes, because you are at the posted limit
explanation: The basic speed law measures your speed against existing conditions, not against the sign, so a legal number can still be an illegal speed in fog.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law prohibits driving at a speed that is greater than reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.

question: Why does the handbook link speed to the time you have to react?
choices: Higher speeds shorten your braking distance
Speed has no effect on reaction time
Higher speeds improve your field of vision
The higher the speed, the less time you have to spot hazards and judge other vehicles
explanation: The handbook explains that the higher the speed, the less time you have to spot hazards, judge the speed of other vehicles and act to avoid mistakes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The higher the speed, the less time you have to spot hazards, judge the speed of other vehicles, and act to avoid personal mistakes and those of other drivers.

question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed on an interstate in West Virginia is:
choices: 75 mph
70 mph
65 mph
55 mph
explanation: The designated interstate limit is a maximum of 70 mph unless otherwise posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Interstate - Maximum Speed 70mph unless otherwise posted

question: Unless otherwise posted, the designated speed limit in a business or residential area is:
choices: 35 mph
45 mph
25 mph
15 mph
explanation: Business and residential areas carry a designated limit of 25 mph, reflecting the number of driveways, parked cars and pedestrians there.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Business or Residential Areas - 25mph

question: You are on an open county highway with no posted sign in sight. What speed applies?
choices: 70 mph
45 mph
25 mph
55 mph
explanation: The designated limit for an open county highway is 55 mph unless otherwise posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Open County Highway - 55mph - unless otherwise posted

question: Which of these designated speed limits is NOT correct?
choices: School zone with children present - 25 mph
Interstate - 70 mph maximum unless otherwise posted
Open county highway - 55 mph unless otherwise posted
Business or residential area - 25 mph
explanation: A school zone is 15 mph while children are present along the roadway; 25 mph is the business and residential figure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: School Zone (while children are present along the roadway) - 15mph

question: A school zone extends how far along the street or highway from the school grounds?
choices: 500 feet
125 feet
100 feet
250 feet
explanation: A school zone is all school property plus any abutting street or highway extending 125 feet along it from the school grounds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: A school zone is all school property, including school grounds, and/or any street or highway abutting the school grounds and extending 125 feet along the street or highway from the school grounds.

question: You have just passed the edge of the school grounds and the children are behind you. When does the school zone end?
choices: At the next intersection
When you can no longer see the school
125 feet along the street or highway from the school grounds
At the school property line
explanation: The zone includes the abutting street or highway for 125 feet beyond the school grounds, so the restriction continues past the property line.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: A school zone is all school property, including school grounds, and/or any street or highway abutting the school grounds and extending 125 feet along the street or highway from the school grounds.

question: How far before a turn must you signal?
choices: At least 500 feet
At least 100 feet
At least 50 feet
At least 200 feet
explanation: The handbook says to signal at least 100 feet before you plan to turn, and to get into the habit of signalling every time you make a change.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Get into the habit of signaling every time you make a change.  Signal at least 100 feet before you plan to turn.

question: Which of these does NOT require a turn signal?
choices: Pulling away from the curb
Entering or leaving an interstate
Coming to a stop in your own lane in slow traffic
Changing lanes
explanation: The handbook lists changing lanes, turning at an intersection, entering or leaving an interstate, pulling away from the curb and pulling over as the moves needing a signal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Other drivers expect you to continue traveling in the same direction.  By using your turn signals, you let them know that you intend to turn or change lanes.

question: You intend to turn at the second street, just beyond the intersection ahead. When should you signal?
choices: As early as possible, to give maximum warning
Only after you have crossed the first intersection and begun the turn
Signalling is optional beyond an intersection
Not so soon that drivers think you are turning at the first intersection
explanation: Signalling too soon makes drivers at the first intersection think you are turning there and pull into your path, while signalling too late leaves those behind you no time to react.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you plan to turn beyond an intersection, do not confuse other drivers by signaling too soon.

question: The handbook's rule about speed and turning is to:
choices: Coast into the turn and brake at its midpoint
Slow down before making the turn and not brake while turning
Brake steadily throughout the turn
Accelerate through the turn to stay stable
explanation: Slowing before the turn and not braking while turning keeps the vehicle settled; braking mid-turn shifts weight and reduces grip exactly when you need it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Slow down before making turns.  Do not brake while turning.

question: You complete a right turn into a two-lane road. Which lane should you end up in?
choices: The left lane, so you can pass sooner
Either lane, as long as you signal
The proper lane, which is the nearest lane to the right
Whichever lane is emptier
explanation: The rule is to always finish turning in the proper lane; drifting into the far lane crosses the path of traffic that expects you to stay right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Always fi nish turning in the proper lane.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the handbook's rules for turns?
choices: Prepare for the turn rather than deciding at the last moment
Check traffic to the front and rear and watch for pedestrians
Check the blind spot by glancing over the proper shoulder
Decide whether to turn at the last moment so you keep your options open
explanation: The handbook says to prepare for the turn and not make decisions to turn at the last moment, so deliberately leaving the decision late is the one option it contradicts.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Before entering the turning lane, signal, look in the mirrors, and check the blind spot by glancing over the proper shoulder.

question: While waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, your front wheels should be:
choices: Turned hard left against the kerb
Pointed straight ahead
Turned to the left, ready for the turn
Turned slightly right
explanation: The handbook says not to turn the wheels to the left while waiting, because a bump from behind could push your vehicle into oncoming traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When waiting to turn left, do not turn the wheels to the left.  Otherwise, a bump from behind could push your vehicle into oncoming traffi  c.

question: Why does it matter which way your wheels point while you wait to turn left?
choices: Angled wheels make the turn slower to complete
Angled wheels obscure your view of oncoming traffic
If you are hit from behind, angled wheels send you into oncoming traffic
Angled wheels wear the tyres unevenly
explanation: A bump from behind could push your vehicle into oncoming traffic if the wheels are already turned left; straight wheels send you forward into the intersection instead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When waiting to turn left, do not turn the wheels to the left.  Otherwise, a bump from behind could push your vehicle into oncoming traffi  c.

question: It is against the law to turn your vehicle around near the crest of a hill unless you can be seen by a vehicle approaching within:
choices: 500 feet in either direction
100 feet in either direction
200 feet in either direction
1,000 feet in either direction
explanation: A turnaround is illegal near a curve or hill crest where you cannot be seen by another vehicle approaching within 500 feet in either direction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: it is against the law to turn your vehicle around near a curve, near the crest of a hill where you cannot be seen by another vehicle approaching within 500 feet in either direction, or where signs  prohibit turning.

question: You have missed your turn and the only wide spot is just over the brow of a hill. What does the law require?
choices: Reverse back over the crest instead
Do not turn around there, because approaching drivers cannot see you in time
Turn around quickly while no vehicle is visible
Turn around with your hazard lights on
explanation: Turning around near the crest of a hill where an approaching vehicle within 500 feet could not see you is against the law, and hazard lights do not change that.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: it is against the law to turn your vehicle around near a curve, near the crest of a hill where you cannot be seen by another vehicle approaching within 500 feet in either direction, or where signs  prohibit turning.

question: Before backing up, you should:
choices: Check completely around the vehicle for people and other obstacles
Check the rear view mirror only
Rely on the reversing camera alone
Sound the horn and reverse slowly
explanation: The handbook says to check completely around your vehicle for people and obstacles, look front, sides and rear, and keep looking to the rear while backing rather than depending on the mirror.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Before backing, check completely around your vehicle for people and/or other obstacles.  You should look to the front, sides and rear and continue to look to the rear while backing. Do not depend on your mirror.

question: Which of these is NOT acceptable according to the handbook?
choices: Backing slowly into the proper traffic lane
Backing across other traffic lanes or through an intersection
Backing into a parallel parking space
Looking to the rear while backing
explanation: You must never back across other traffic lanes or through an intersection; backing into a parallel parking space is the stated exception to backing in a traffic lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: It is not advisable to back up while in a traffi  c lane, except for backing into a parallel parking space.  Never back across other traffi  c lanes or through an intersection.

question: You are reversing out of a residential driveway. What does the handbook single out as the special risk?
choices: Traffic signals you cannot see
Your mirrors misting up
Children who may have run behind the vehicle
Damage to the kerb
explanation: Drivers are told to be extra watchful when backing in or out of a driveway for children who may have run behind the vehicle, where no mirror will show them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: As a driver, be extra careful in residential areas, school zones and at times and places where children are likely to be around.

question: Vehicles must always be parked:
choices: Facing the same direction as traffic moves on that side of the street
Facing oncoming traffic so you can see it
At any angle, provided the vehicle is off the travelled portion
Facing downhill where possible
explanation: Parking in the direction traffic moves on that side of the street means you enter and leave the space without crossing into opposing traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which of these is NOT required when you park and leave your vehicle?

Leaving the engine running if you will only be a moment
Turning off the engine
Setting the parking or emergency brake
explanation: The handbook requires the engine off and the parking brake set whenever you park and leave the vehicle, and adds that you should lock it and take your keys.

source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road

question: You are about to open your door into the street after parking. What does the handbook warn about?
choices: You must never exit on the street side under any circumstances
Opening the door releases the parking brake
Bicycles, motorcycles or larger vehicles passing may not see your door in time
The door may trigger the alarm
explanation: Getting out on the street side can be dangerous because passing bicycles, motorcycles or larger vehicles may not see you in time to avoid hitting your open door, or you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Getting out of your vehicle on the street side can be dangerous. Always look carefully  for bicycles, motorcycles, or larger vehicles that might be passing. The drivers may not see you in time to keep from hitting your open door, or you.

No closer than 15 feet
No closer than 10 feet
No closer than 20 feet

A kerb painted white outside a shop
Upon any bridge or elevated structure or in a highway tunnel
In front of a wheelchair ramp or curb cut
explanation: The listed prohibitions include bridges and tunnels, wheelchair ramps and curb cuts, and 20 feet from a served mailbox; the handbook notes a no-parking kerb may be painted yellow, not white.

question: When you park or stop on a grade, you should turn the front wheels:
choices: Straight ahead and rely on the transmission
Away from the curb so the vehicle rolls clear
In whichever direction is easiest to drive out
To the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll
explanation: Turning the front wheels to the curb side of the highway means that if the vehicle creeps, the wheels bring it against the kerb instead of into traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

source.sourceQuote: If you park or stop on a grade, turn the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll.  Be sure to set the emergency or parking brake.

question: Besides turning the wheels, what else does the handbook require when parking on a grade?
choices: Setting the emergency or parking brake
Leaving the vehicle in neutral
Chocking a wheel
Parking with two wheels on the sidewalk
explanation: You must be sure to set the emergency or parking brake, and the handbook adds that in an automatic you put the selector in park to reinforce it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: When you have finished parallel parking, your wheels should be within how far of the curb?
choices: 24 inches
36 inches
18 inches
12 inches
explanation: The handbook requires the wheels to be parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb, and the vehicle to face the direction of traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

subtopic: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
question: You have parallel parked on the left side of a one-way street. Which curb do the wheels have to be within 18 inches of?
choices: The right curb
Either curb
Neither — the 18-inch rule only applies on the right
The left curb
explanation: When parallel parking on the left side of the road the wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb, and the vehicle still faces the direction of traffic.

question: The handbook's recommended method for judging following distance is:
choices: Two car lengths at any speed
Half the speedometer reading in feet
The three-to-four second rule
One car length for every 10 mph
explanation: The best way to assure proper following distance is the three-to-four second rule, which stays correct at every speed without any arithmetic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The best way to assure proper following distance is to use the three-to-four second rule.

question: The vehicle ahead passes a bridge abutment and you reach it while still saying 'one thousand two'. What does that tell you?
choices: You have a safe gap
You are following too far back
The test only works at low speed
You are following too closely
explanation: If you reach the fixed object before you finish saying 'one thousand three', you are driving too closely and need to drop back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

question: Which of these is NOT a suitable fixed object for counting following distance?
choices: The vehicle ahead of you
A signpost
An overpass
A bridge abutment
explanation: The object has to be fixed — the handbook names a signpost, tree, overpass or bridge abutment — because a moving vehicle gives you no reference point.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

question: If it is dark or raining, your following distance should be at least:
choices: Four seconds
Two seconds
Three seconds
Six seconds
explanation: The handbook raises the minimum to at least four seconds when it is dark or raining, because both sight and grip are reduced.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If it is dark or raining, the distance should be at least four seconds.

question: There is ice and snow on the road. How far back should you stay from the vehicle in front?
choices: The same as in dry conditions
At least six seconds
At least four seconds
At least three seconds
explanation: On ice or snow you should stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front, double the usual dry-weather figure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

question: A driver is keeping a six-second gap. Which condition does the handbook match to that distance?
choices: Dry daylight driving
Following a motorcycle in the dry
Ice or snow
Dark or raining
explanation: Six seconds is the figure the handbook gives for ice or snow; four seconds covers dark or rain and three to four is the general baseline.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

question: Besides checking your mirrors, what must you do before changing lanes?
choices: Sound your horn
Flash your headlights
Slow to below the speed limit
Check over your shoulder for the blind spot
explanation: A head check over the left or right shoulder is needed because mirrors do not cover the blind spot where another vehicle can sit unseen.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Check over your left or right shoulder (head check) to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

question: Where does the handbook say you must NOT change lanes?
choices: In an intersection or at a railroad crossing
On a four-lane divided highway
Within 100 feet of a driveway
Anywhere broken white lines are present
explanation: The rule is DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing, both places where vehicles enter your path from directions you are not watching.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing.

question: You have checked your mirrors and your blind spot and both are clear. What is the remaining check the handbook lists?
choices: Whether you are exceeding the minimum speed
Whether another driver is also moving into the same lane
Whether your tyres are correctly inflated
Whether the lane ends within a mile
explanation: The handbook adds a check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane — the vehicle converging from the far side that neither mirror nor head check covers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Check over your left or right shoulder (head check) to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper clears their front bumper
After counting five seconds
When the passed driver flashes their lights
When you can see the front of the passed vehicle, both headlights, in your rear view mirror
explanation: Seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear view mirror is the handbook's proof that you have left it enough space to keep braking distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal and return to the proper lane when you see the front of the vehicle (both headlights) you have passed in your rear view mirror. Passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

question: Passing on the right is:
choices: Not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing
Always permissible on a multi-lane road
Permissible if the vehicle ahead is turning left
Permissible at any intersection
explanation: The handbook says passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal and return to the proper lane when you see the front of the vehicle (both headlights) you have passed in your rear view mirror. Passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

question: You are about to overtake on a two-lane highway at night. What does the handbook allow you to do to alert the driver ahead?
choices: Sound a long horn blast only
Blink your headlights
Flash your hazard lights
Use your high beams continuously
explanation: You should sound your horn to alert the driver ahead, and at night you can also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Move left when clear and sound your horn to alert the driver ahead that you are passing. At night you can also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
question: Passing is prohibited within how many feet of an intersection?
choices: 200 feet
500 feet
100 feet
50 feet
explanation: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of an intersection, because a vehicle can emerge into the lane you are occupying.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which of these is NOT a place where the handbook prohibits passing?
choices: Within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel or underpass
On a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic
When the solid yellow line is in your lane
On a straight, level road with a broken yellow line on your side
explanation: A broken yellow line on your side of a clear, straight road is exactly where passing is allowed when it is safe; the other three are on the prohibited list.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
